role: Independent metadata and primary-source review; live model acquisition files were neither read nor modified.
source_retrieval: GitHub connector fetched the three pinned text files. Source text was stored with the tool-added extra terminal newline removed to match decoded response character counts. MIT license is included. No remote source was executed.

verified_library_behavior.claim: HDF5.jl maps Julia dimension tuples to reversed HDF5 dimensions and maps HDF5 dimensions back by reversal.
Base.size of a dataspace gets native HDF5 extent dimensions and returns _from_h5_dims; get_extent_dims uses the same conversion.
Official HDF5.jl documentation explains Julia column-major versus common C/Python row-major array interoperability and dimension reversal.

independently_verified_local_metadata.basis: Prior independent geometry metadata review; no live acquisition read.

conditional_interpretation.condition: If the versioned Zenodo HDF5 file uses the semantics of the same-basename Overthrust file read by the pinned JUDI example, with HDF5.jl dimension-reversal convention.
conditional_interpretation.Julia_model_shape_order: (x,y,z) = (801,801,207), matching the stored one-dimensional n vector; reversing dimensions does not reverse the values of a 1D vector.
conditional_interpretation.stored_C_shape_order: (z,y,x) = (207,801,801). The middle y/x dimensions are equal, so shape alone cannot distinguish their names; JUDI convention supplies the conditional names.
conditional_interpretation.selected_plane: For zero-based z,x, stored-plane[z,x] equals Julia_m[x+1,401,z+1] under this convention. Julia_m[:,401,:] has x-by-z axes; the acquired NumPy plane already has z-by-x axes. It requires no additional transpose for a z-by-x output.
conditional_interpretation.coordinates_if_JUDI_geometry_applies: d is 25 metres in x,y,z and o is zero; plane y=10,000m, x=0..20,000m, z=0..5,150m at node coordinates. These are interpreted coordinates, not new embedded HDF5 unit metadata.
conditional_interpretation.stored_m_units_if_JUDI_semantics_apply: Squared slowness s^2/km^2, numerically equivalent to ms^2/m^2. Physical velocity would be 1/sqrt(m) km/s or 1000/sqrt(m) m/s.

explicit_limits: JUDI example names an FTP URL and the same basename; no checksum or immutable file identity links that FTP file to Zenodo file UUID 436595b8-ed4b-4e1d-8991-e63608dcc169.

No original CD1 velocity-grid equality or rounding identity is established. The original grid has 187 rows in its README while this stored HDF5 grid has 207; dimension reversal alone does not explain those 20 additional rows.

No Julia package installation, reader execution, exact writer/version provenance or runtime validation of the pinned JUDI example was performed. The example was authored in 2017 and retained at the pinned current repository commit; compatibility with the current constructor API was not tested.
Physical unit/axis interpretation is supported by primary software-use context and an explicit consistency check, not directly encoded unit/axis attributes in the inspected HDF5 metadata.

No live plane artifact was read, converted, cropped, smoothed or used for a wave/PDE run. No independent geological site, untouched confirmation, recovery advantage or physics-acceptance claim follows.
A later derivative model must retain the exact acquired stored plane and separately identify the interpretation assumption, arithmetic transformation, row selection, units and hashes.
